title: Grateful Dead Live at Alfred College on 1970-05-01
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v1.5 ->Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC
source: Source 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD Source 2: SBD ->Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD Source 3: SBD -> Master Reel -> Reel-> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Stellar May 1 1970 acoustic‑electric show captured on a superb soundboard mix, with crystal‑clear folk gems and a fiery electric set despite a few tape quirks.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that delivers an exceptionally clear acoustic half – highlighted by “Me & My Uncle,” “Mama Tried,” “Deep Elem Blues,” and a legendary “Speedway Boogie” – while the electric side burns with “Hard to Handle,” “High Time,” and “The Other One.”  Reviewers rave about Jerry’s guitar tone, Pigpen’s front‑man presence, and even NRPS guests adding sweet harmonies, though a handful note low‑frequency oversaturation on Cryptical Envelopment and minor mic noise on “I Know You Rider.”  Overall the performance is regarded as one of the best early‑1970 shows and the tape quality is judged good to excellent.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise both performance and sound; show quality scores ~4.6/5, recording quality ~4.2/5, yielding a weighted average of ~4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo soundboard mix is crystal clear on the acoustic set; occasional harsh low‑frequency oversaturation (Cryptical Envelopment source 3), minor mic noise on “I Know You Rider,” and a cardboard‑box beat artifact in the electric portion, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic first set is described as pure gold and uniquely arranged, followed by an electric second set that’s fiery yet a touch shorter than later shows; some reviewers note missing or cut portions but the overall pacing is praised.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is repeatedly called perfect; his occasional electric lead on acoustic numbers noted, plus a disputed vocal line on “I Know You Rider.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh is mentioned loading gear and as the source of alternate lyrics on “I Know You Rider”; no specific bass performance remarks.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drumming is referenced in a personal anecdote about loading wagons; no detailed drum critique.
